rationale: PICOS B (Pete 2026-10-07): studies of what EXISTING forest does or what its loss costs are evidence for protection / community forestry (which keeps the forest standing), not for planting or regeneration within a project horizon. Kept in their own family row (protection; mangrove_coastal for existing-mangrove studies), out of the NbS roll-up and out of every other family.

PICOS B mirrored for wetlands (2026-10-08): studies of what EXISTING wetlands/floodplains do are evidence for keeping/restoring them, not for creation; kept in the restoration family row, out of the roll-up.

Pete 2026-10-16: a restored wetland falling short of an INTACT one is not harm and the comparison is not useful - 'a more sensible baseline is needed (e.g. compared to what was there before the wetland was created or restored, or how the wetland increases biodiversity in the landscape, catchment or meta-population / ecological network, how it could increase landscape connectivity)'. These units are kept as a recovery note and never set a class.
Same rule as wetland reference_wetland (Pete 2026-10-16): restored-vs-intact-reference shortfalls are a recovery note, not an effect of restoring.
Coastal marsh evidence measured on EXISTING marsh belongs in the coastal family row, not the rewetting one - mirrors how existing-mangrove studies route to mangrove_coastal in forest restoration.
Silvopasture measured against ungrazed native forest is a conservation benchmark, not an intervention counterfactual (Pete 2026-10-16 baseline ruling).
A buffer measured against undisturbed lakeshore forest is a recovery shortfall, not an effect of establishing the buffer (Pete 2026-10-16).
